title: Cramer's Rule OQ-05-OQ-02: Similarity is an Equivalence Relation, Preserved by Polynomial Evaluation
description: Answers the parent entry's first open question: matrix similarity IsSimilar M N := ∃ U, N = U M U⁻¹ is an equivalence relation (adds symmetry and transitivity to the parent's reflexivity, bundled as Equivalence and Setoid instances), and it is a congruence for the entire polynomial functional calculus — if M ~ N then p(M) ~ p(N) for every polynomial p ∈ R[X]. The mechanism is that conjugation by a fixed unit is an R-algebra homomorphism conjAlgHom U of the matrix ring, so Polynomial.aeval (being natural in the algebra) commutes with it. Capstone: similar matrices have p(M) and p(N) with equal characteristic polynomials for all p. Over an arbitrary commutative ring. 15 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Similarity — the relation N = U M U⁻¹ between matrices representing the same endomorphism in different bases — is the central equivalence of linear operator theory, developed through the 19th-century invariant theory of Cayley, Sylvester, and Frobenius and culminating in the rational and Jordan canonical forms. That similarity is an equivalence relation is the structural fact that makes 'the operator up to change of basis' well-defined: the equivalence classes are precisely the isomorphism classes of finitely generated modules over R[X] (the module structure where X acts by the matrix). A deeper property is functoriality under the polynomial functional calculus: because conjugation by a fixed unit is an algebra automorphism of the matrix ring, it commutes with every polynomial expression, so p(M) and p(N) are similar whenever M and N are. This is why spectral data — eigenvalues, and more generally the characteristic polynomial of any polynomial in the operator — are basis-independent, and it underlies the simultaneous-triangularization and functional-calculus arguments used throughout operator theory and representation theory.
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry (cramers-rule-oq-05) defined conj U N = U N U⁻¹ and IsSimilar M N := ∃ U, N = conj U M, proving only reflexivity. Its first open question asks: prove that similarity is an equivalence relation (symmetry and transitivity) and that IsSimilar is preserved by polynomial evaluation p(M). This entry resolves both.
overview.text: Similarity is reflexive (conjugate by the identity, from the parent), symmetric (if N = U M U⁻¹ then M = U⁻¹ N U, witness U⁻¹), and transitive (if N = U M U⁻¹ and P = V N V⁻¹ then P = (VU) M (VU)⁻¹, witness V*U). These are bundled into an Equivalence and a Setoid. For polynomial evaluation, the key is that conj U : Matrix n n R → Matrix n n R preserves +, *, 1, 0, and scalars, hence is an R-algebra homomorphism conjAlgHom U. Polynomial.aeval is natural with respect to algebra homomorphisms (aeval_algHom_apply: aeval (f x) p = f (aeval x p)), so aeval (conj U M) p = conj U (aeval M p), i.e. p(U M U⁻¹) = U p(M) U⁻¹. Therefore M ~ N implies p(M) ~ p(N) for every p, with the same conjugating unit. Combining with characteristic-polynomial invariance gives the capstone: p(M) and p(N) have equal characteristic polynomials for all polynomials p.
overview.proofStrategy: Part I proves the five preservation laws conj_mul (uses U⁻¹ U = 1 to cancel the inner factor), conj_one, conj_add, conj_zero, conj_algebraMap (uses Algebra.commutes that scalars are central), and assembles them into the algebra homomorphism conjAlgHom U with a definitional apply lemma. Part II records the cancellation conj U⁻¹ (conj U N) = N and the composition law conj V (conj U N) = conj (V*U) N. Part III derives IsSimilar.symm and IsSimilar.trans from these and bundles refl/symm/trans into isSimilar_equivalence and isSimilarSetoid. Part IV proves aeval_conj via Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply on conjAlgHom, then IsSimilar.aeval by destructuring the similarity witness. Part V re-derives IsSimilar.charpoly_eq from Matrix.charpoly_units_conj and combines it with IsSimilar.aeval to give the capstone IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval_eq.
keyInsights: The right abstraction for 'similarity is preserved by p(M)' is that conjugation by a unit is an R-algebra homomorphism — once conjAlgHom U is in hand, the whole functional-calculus compatibility is a single application of Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply, with no polynomial induction written by hand
Symmetry and transitivity reduce to unit arithmetic: the witnesses are U⁻¹ and the product V*U, and the proofs are pure associativity plus the unit cancellations U⁻¹ U = 1 and (V*U)⁻¹ = U⁻¹ V⁻¹

Conjugation preserves addition (U(a+b)U⁻¹ = UaU⁻¹ + UbU⁻¹), so it is a full ring/algebra homomorphism, not merely a monoid homomorphism — this is exactly what Mathlib's ConjAct provides only as a MulDistribMulAction, so the algebra-homomorphism packaging here adds the additive structure
The result holds over any commutative ring R, so it applies to matrices over ℤ and polynomial rings; the same conjugating unit U works simultaneously for M ~ N and for p(M) ~ p(N)

A homomorphism is all that aeval naturality needs. conjAlgHom U is only an AlgHom (a one-directional structure-preserving map), not the invertible AlgEquiv that this entry's sibling `cramers-rule-oq-05-oq-01` constructs for the same conjugation. Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply requires nothing more than an algebra homomorphism, so packaging conj U as an AlgEquiv there is strictly stronger than what the aeval-preservation argument itself demands — the extra invertibility only pays for itself if one later wants the automorphism structure (e.g. to transport minpoly, an open question of both entries) rather than just the congruence p(M) ~ p(N).
prerequisites: Units of the matrix ring (Matrix n n R)ˣ and the cancellations Units.inv_mul, Units.mul_inv, mul_inv_rev
R-algebra homomorphisms of a noncommutative R-algebra (AlgHom) and that scalars are central (Algebra.commutes)
Polynomial evaluation Polynomial.aeval and its naturality Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply
Equivalence and Setoid structures; the parent entry's conj and IsSimilar definitions

conclusion.summary: Fully machine-verified resolution of cramers-rule-oq-05's first open question over an arbitrary commutative ring: matrix similarity is an equivalence relation (isSimilar_equivalence, isSimilarSetoid) and a congruence for the polynomial functional calculus (IsSimilar.aeval: M ~ N ⟹ p(M) ~ p(N)), because conjugation by a unit is an R-algebra homomorphism (conjAlgHom). Capstone: similar matrices yield p(M), p(N) with equal characteristic polynomials for every polynomial p. Zero axioms, zero sorries.
conclusion.implications: Establishing similarity as an equivalence relation is the prerequisite for quotienting matrices by change of basis, the setting for canonical-form theory (rational and Jordan forms) and for the classification of finitely generated R[X]-modules. The functional-calculus compatibility p(M) ~ p(N) is the abstract reason spectral invariants are basis-independent: it feeds directly into simultaneous-triangularization arguments, the spectral mapping theorem, and the fact that any polynomial in an operator is again well-defined up to similarity. Packaging conjugation as an algebra homomorphism gives a reusable API for transporting any aeval-expressible identity across a change of basis.
openQuestions: Show the minimal polynomial is a similarity invariant: minpoly of U M U⁻¹ equals minpoly of M, and more generally that the R[X]-module structures induced by similar matrices are isomorphic (cf. cayley-hamilton-minpoly)
Promote conjAlgHom to an AlgEquiv (with inverse conjAlgHom U⁻¹) and identify the resulting group homomorphism (Matrix n n R)ˣ → (Matrix n n R ≃ₐ[R] Matrix n n R) as the inner-automorphism map
Prove that similar matrices have equal rank and, over a field, the same eigenvalues with multiplicity, deducing these from the characteristic-polynomial equality established here

crossReferences.description: Directly answers the parent entry's first open question. The parent defined conj and IsSimilar and proved reflexivity plus det/trace/charpoly invariance; this entry adds symmetry, transitivity, the Equivalence/Setoid packaging, and preservation of similarity under polynomial evaluation.

The polynomial-evaluation compatibility proved here is the companion to minimal-polynomial invariance under conjugation; both express that polynomial data of a matrix descends to the underlying linear map.

sections.title: Imports, docstring, and variable setup
sections.summary: Imports the parent entry (for conj and IsSimilar) and Mathlib's polynomial-algebra library. Opens the CramersRuleOQ05 namespace to reuse conj, conj_apply, and IsSimilar. Declares universe-polymorphic variables n (finite decidable index) and R (commutative ring); everything holds over an arbitrary commutative ring.

sections.title: Part I: Conjugation by a unit is an algebra homomorphism
sections.summary: Proves the five preservation laws conj_mul (inner U⁻¹ U = 1 cancellation), conj_one, conj_add, conj_zero, and conj_algebraMap (scalars are central via Algebra.commutes), and packages them into conjAlgHom U : Matrix n n R →ₐ[R] Matrix n n R with a definitional apply lemma conjAlgHom_apply.

sections.title: Part II: Cancellation and the group law of conjugation
sections.summary: Records conj_inv_conj (conjugating by U then U⁻¹ is the identity) and conj_conj (nested conjugations compose along the product of units: V (U N U⁻¹) V⁻¹ = (VU) N (VU)⁻¹), the arithmetic behind symmetry and transitivity.

sections.title: Part III: Similarity is an equivalence relation
sections.summary: Proves IsSimilar.symm (witness U⁻¹) and IsSimilar.trans (witness V*U) and bundles them with the parent's reflexivity into isSimilar_equivalence and the isSimilarSetoid Setoid on Matrix n n R.

sections.title: Part IV: Similarity is preserved by polynomial evaluation
sections.summary: Proves aeval_conj (p(U M U⁻¹) = U p(M) U⁻¹, via Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply on conjAlgHom) and IsSimilar.aeval (M ~ N ⟹ p(M) ~ p(N) for every polynomial p), showing similarity is a congruence for the polynomial functional calculus.

sections.title: Part V: Capstone — equal characteristic polynomials of polynomial values
sections.summary: Re-derives IsSimilar.charpoly_eq from Matrix.charpoly_units_conj and combines it with IsSimilar.aeval to prove IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval_eq: for similar M, N and every polynomial p, the matrices p(M) and p(N) have equal characteristic polynomials.

sections.title: Part VI: Summary
sections.summary: Tabulates the new results and explains that the parent showed the classical invariants are constant on a similarity class, while this entry shows the underlying relation is a genuine equivalence relation and a congruence for the entire polynomial functional calculus.
